To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
novel words are integrated into the mental lexical network over time.

(1) novel word meanings are integrated over time, (2) the extent of integration is modulated by study modality, (3) words studied in written format are integrated most, and (4) the process of integration does not differ between the two study modalities.

(1) novel words are not immediately integrated into the mental lexical network, but require time; (2) the integration of novel words into the mental lexical system is facilitated by studying in a written format; (3) this integration is not modality-specific, as both written and spoken novel words are able to benefit from the study modality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the human brain processes new information.
how the brain stores information about the meaning of novel words and how the meaning of these words can be retrieved from memory.
the acquisition and integration of novel word meanings in the adult brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the overnight integration of word meanings is a time-consuming process that is modulated by study modality.
the CLS model is a very good explanation of the learning process of word meanings, and that studying with a written format is better than studying with a spoken format.
the CLS account of word learning is not supported by our data, but that the data are compatible with the CLS account, and that they also support the idea of an overnight semantic integration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
learning word meanings is a gradual process and that studying in the written format is beneficial to this process.
the integration of novel word meanings is a gradual process that is facilitated by studying with written definitions.
learning word meanings requires time, but studying in a written format facilitates semantic integration more than a spoken format.
The main takeaway from our work is that
semantic integration of newly learned words is a slow process, which is modulated by the learning modality used during study.
the CLS account of learning is not only applicable to the learning of word forms but also to learning word meanings.

novel words are not fully integrated into the mental word lexicon immediately after study, but that this process takes some time and that studying in a written format may be more beneficial for the integration of word meanings than studying in spoken modality.
